> Runtime: median of --runs measured runs (default 7); the 95% confidence interval, standard deviation and any outlier samples are in latest.json.
> Peak memory: highest sampled working set while the program ran, per language; interpreted languages therefore include their VM.

> Cold build: median of --compile-repeats cold builds (default 3) from a fresh cache directory for lsaca; one --compile-repeats median for gcc and rustc. In fallback build mode the lsaca cold column is the emit-c + gcc total.

## Independent oracle verification

scripts/oracles.py holds independent Python reference implementations of every workload. Before measuring, the harness recomputed 22 program checksums and 39 data-scale checksums from those references; mismatches: 0.

A mismatch aborts the run before any measurement is taken, so a published result always has all language outputs agreeing with the independent reference.

### v2.0 acceptance targets

| metric | v1.7 | v2.0 | target | status |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| smallest single-file cold build (vec_memory) | 0.983 (hashmap_i64) | 0.379 (vec_memory) | 0.35-0.5 s | within target |
| cached build, fib | 16.3 ms | 44.8 ms | about 15 ms | outside target |
| compile_large cold build | 1.837 s | 2.023 s | <= 2.5 x the C reference build | needs C reference (measure separately) |
| runtime within 1.4x of C | n/a | 13 of 22 above target | none above target unless documented | document: fib_iter, loop_sum, string_build, vec_memory, matrix_multiply, binary_trees, binary_trees_refs, string_split, mandelbrot, hashmap_wordcount, array_wordcount, string_unicode, hashmap_i64 |

Targets are the v2.0 performance acceptance criteria: every measured aspect within 1.4x of C (or documented), a hello-sized cold build of 0.35-0.5 s, a cached build of about 15 ms, and compile_large at no more than 2.5x the reference C build. The cold-build proxy is the smallest single-file workload in the suite; once a dedicated hello workload is added, use it instead.

| string_build | 2.44 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| vec_memory | 1.44 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| matrix_multiply | 1.43 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| binary_trees | 10.31 | by-value workload: each recursive step builds and returns a subtree by value, so deep copies are part of the measured workload by design; `binary_trees_refs` is the comparable reference-traversal variant. |
| binary_trees_refs | 2.33 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| string_split | 1.91 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| mandelbrot | 1.65 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| hashmap_wordcount | 1.43 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| array_wordcount | 1.51 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| string_unicode | 3.06 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| hashmap_i64 | 1.42 | to be documented in Fairness notes |

Brought under the target by Phase D: iterator_pipeline (2.48x -> 1.15x), fn_pipeline (1.42x -> 1.40x), hashmap_string (1.49x -> 1.07x).

Known semantic limitations (documented, not chased):

- `binary_trees`: by-value workload: each recursive step builds and returns a subtree by value, so deep copies are part of the measured workload by design; `binary_trees_refs` is the comparable reference-traversal variant.
